b: “Nothing happens until something moves” is the title of Robert Ringer’s book on action, and it means exactly what it says: nothing in your life, your career, or your pipeline changes until you make the first move. Most people wait for permission, certainty, or the perfect moment. None of those ever arrive. The alternative to moving isn’t safety. It’s regret.
Key Takeaways: Nothing Happens Until Something Moves
The line is the title of Robert Ringer’s book “Action! Nothing Happens Until Something Moves.” It’s often misattributed to Einstein.
The sales version belongs to Red Motley: “Nothing happens until somebody sells something.”
People don’t stay stuck because of fear. They stay stuck because they doubt their ability to figure things out as they go.
The ability to figure it out is latent in everyone. It activates only when you make a conscious decision to move.
You won’t remember what things cost. You will remember, painfully, the things you didn’t do.
Don’t be afraid to lose. Be afraid of not trying.
Is there anything worse than living in a constant state of inaction or paralyzing fear? Yes… I believe it’s called a state of regret.
What “Nothing Happens Until Something Moves” Really Means

Let’s get the attribution right, because the internet usually doesn’t. “Nothing happens until something moves” is the title of Robert Ringer’s book on taking action, and though the line gets credited to Albert Einstein in a thousand motivational posts, it’s Ringer’s book that says it all.
Physics agrees with him either way: an object at rest stays at rest until a force acts on it. Your career obeys the same law.

Salespeople have their own version of the line, and it’s older than both of us. Red Motley, the legendary publisher of Parade magazine, put it this way: “Nothing happens until somebody sells something.”

No factory runs, no truck rolls, no paycheck clears until someone, somewhere, makes a sale. Selling is the first mover of the entire economy, which means if you’re in sales, you are the something that has to move.
For something to happen in our life, we must make something happen. We must instigate.
The People Who Refuse to Move

Years ago I was invited to do a full day of training on internet marketing, a favorite pastime to my sales training business. In that training, I spoke to many people who simply refused to believe that the internet was a viable option for them to make money. They didn’t believe ‘they’ could make money online. Some refused to believe the internet was even growing, and this was in the face of record-shattering online sales numbers I put right in front of them.
After the workshop, a few people shared their hesitations with me. The excuses were vast, varied, and elaborately defended. Even facing overwhelming evidence, they refused to move.

I’m watching the same movie again right now, except this time the subject is AI. I wrote a book about artificial intelligence and selling, and everywhere I go I meet salespeople constructing elaborate cases for why AI doesn’t apply to them, why their business is different, why they’ll wait and see.
They are the same people from my internet marketing workshop, separated by fifteen years and making the same choice. The technology was never the point. The refusal to move was.

Age has taught me not to argue, but to accept and respect the opinions and decisions of others no matter how misguided I think they may be. Nonetheless, that obstinate disposition got me thinking about why some people make money and others don’t.
The Latent Ability in All of Us

Every person carries with them the ability to do great things, but what stops them? Fear? No, I don’t think so. I think everyone wants to be successful, but they simply don’t believe they have the necessary ‘cognitive tools’ to pull it off. They doubt their own intellect or their ability to construct their own reality.

But I’m convinced that somewhere in each of us is the latent, yet to emerge, ability to figure things out as we go along. The problem is that each of us is unable to tap into that ability unless we make a conscious decision to activate those cognitive skills and directionally point them at what we want to happen.
We all have the “profitability gene” within us, but it will remain latent unless we take a bold stance and decide to make something happen.
Knowing the principle is worth nothing. Moving is worth everything. Here is how I coach people to get something moving when they’ve been stuck.

Name the move you’ve been avoiding. Not five moves. One. You already know what it is, because it’s the one that made you uncomfortable just now when you read this sentence. The calls you’re not making. The certification you keep postponing. The conversation with your manager you keep rescheduling. Write it down in plain language.

Shrink it until it’s impossible to fail. The reason you haven’t moved is that you’ve defined the move as the whole mountain. You don’t need to build a personal brand this week; you need to publish one post. You don’t need to transform your pipeline; you need to make ten calls tomorrow morning. Momentum doesn’t care how small the first motion is. Physics only requires that something moves.

Put a date on it and tell someone. A move without a deadline is a wish, and a private commitment is barely a commitment at all. Book it on the calendar and say it out loud to someone who will ask you about it. Accountability is the cheapest performance enhancer ever invented.

Expect the old habits to fight back. The first thing that happens when you start moving is that everything in you that preferred standing still wakes up and objects. That’s not a sign you’re doing it wrong. That’s the signal you’re doing it at all.

Breaking the bad habits that anchored you is part of the move, not a prerequisite for it. And remember that standing still was never actually an option: in the marketplace, change will be forced on you whether you instigate it or not. The only choice you get is whether you’re the one moving or the one being moved.
Is there anything worse than living in a constant state of inaction or paralyzing fear? Yes… I believe it’s called a state of regret.
When the time is near and the Reaper fixes his gaze upon us as we lie on our deathbed drawing our last few breaths, we won’t remember what things cost or how much money we spent.

But we will remember, with painful denial, the things we didn’t do. We will regret all those opportunities and moments of action that we talked ourselves out of. Try as we might, we cannot deny that we passed through life not as active participants but as willing accomplices to inaction.

So I ask you to reach under your bed of dreams and pull out the whims and desires you’ve quietly stowed away when no one was looking. Activate those latent wishes for health, prosperity, and success. Take a small gamble; do something outside your perceived limitation. Don’t be afraid to lose, but be afraid of not trying.

Life is too short to keep doing things we don’t like doing. If your job stinks, make a move. If your relationship stinks, make a move. If your financial situation isn’t what you want it to be, make a move.
If you don’t, what’s the alternative? Ringer said it best: “Nothing happens until something moves.” It’s your move!

Common Questions About “Nothing Happens Until Something Moves”
What does “nothing happens until something moves” mean?

It means that no change, in physics or in life, begins without a first motion, and in your career you are the thing that has to move. Waiting for certainty, permission, or the perfect moment guarantees nothing happens, because none of those ever arrive on their own. The principle applies to everything from making sales calls to changing jobs: name the move, make it small enough to start, and start.
Who said “nothing happens until something moves”?

The line is the title of Robert Ringer’s book “Action! Nothing Happens Until Something Moves.” It is frequently misattributed to Albert Einstein in motivational posts, but Ringer’s book is the source of the phrase as it’s popularly used. The physics behind the idea, an object at rest stays at rest until a force acts on it, belongs to Newton.
What is the sales version of the quote?

“Nothing happens until somebody sells something,” a line attributed to Red Motley, the longtime publisher of Parade magazine. His point was that selling is the first mover of the entire economy: no order means no production, no shipping, no payroll. For salespeople, it’s a reminder that the whole business is waiting on your next move.
How do you take action when you feel stuck?

Name the one move you’ve been avoiding, then shrink it until it’s impossible to fail: one post instead of a personal brand, ten calls instead of a transformed pipeline. Put a date on it and tell someone who will hold you to it. And expect internal resistance when you start; that’s not a warning sign, it’s proof that something finally moved. If you can’t make the move alone, a coach exists to supply the outside force.
